title: Residential Natural Gas Supply — Utility Processing, Supply Start and Contract End Date
content:
**Clause.** After an enrollment under Residential Natural Gas Supply is submitted, the gas utility either accepts it, its confirmation letter date being recorded as the utility confirmation date, or rejects it with one of the utility's rejection reasons. Supply begins on the switch meter read date, which becomes the service start date.

**Contract end date.** For a plan whose term is above 0 months, the contract end date is the day before the same calendar day the term's number of calendar months after the service start date. When that calendar day does not exist in the target month, the last day of that month is used before subtracting the day. A month-to-month plan has no contract end date.

**Rejection.** A rejected enrollment ends permanently; a new enrollment creates a new agreement priced on its own enrollment date.

### Contract end dates worked through (hypothetical service start dates)

| Service start date | Term (months) | Same calendar day after the term | Contract end date |
|---|---|---|---|
| 15 January 2025 | 24 | 15 January 2027 | 14 January 2027 |
| 31 March 2025 | 12 | 31 March 2026 | 30 March 2026 |
| 29 February 2024 | 12 | 29 February 2025 does not exist; last day of February 2025 is 28 February | 27 February 2025 |
| 10 June 2025 | 0 (month-to-month) | — | none |

### Points of judgement

- The confirmation letter date and the service start date are different dates: the first records the utility's acceptance, the second the switch meter read on which supply began.
- A rejected enrollment is never revived; the customer's new enrollment is a new agreement with its own enrollment date and its own pricing.
